source: the house copy standard is the prose; this file is what the linter reads. Edit both in one operation.

markers.name: trailing benefit clause
markers.why: A complete clause ends, then a comma, then a verb-ing tail asserting a benefit. Owners state the fact and stop.

markers.name: fronted participial
markers.why: Sentence opens with a verb-ing phrase before the actor. Actors come first in shop speech.

markers.name: copular abstraction
markers.pattern: \b(is|are|was|were)\s+(all about|designed to|here to|dedicated to|committed to|built to|meant to|about)\b
markers.why: Describes what a service IS rather than what hands do.

markers.name: antithetical polarity
markers.why: not just X but Y. Contrast used for weight where a number or a tool would do.

markers.name: colon then explanation
markers.origin: house 2026-09-13 marker 1, refined after external review
markers.why: A claim pre-announced then unpacked. The defect is the pre-announcement, not the colon: a label-to-value colon (Hours: 9 to 5) is fine.

markers.name: symmetrical tricolon
markers.why: Three equal-weight, equal-length parallel clauses built to be read as a set.

markers.name: symmetrical bicolon
markers.why: Two matched clauses joined by and, same grammar, syllable counts within 2.

markers.name: rhetorical question header
markers.why: Question header simulating customer empathy, answered immediately below.

markers.name: agency gloss
markers.why: Abstract-virtue adjectives stacked on a concrete physical task.

markers.name: tagline headline
markers.why: Short abstract headline working as free-standing ad copy, naming no business, place, price, time or service.

markers.name: label with bolted-on claim
markers.why: A service or section name is the bare noun. No verb phrase, participle, preposition tag or explanation bolted on.

markers.name: flat sentence-length entropy
markers.why: Four or more consecutive prose sentences whose word-count coefficient of variation is under 0.18 where the mean is 14 words or more. CV rather than raw stdev because stdev scales with sentence length: 3.0 on 12-word sentences is 25% variation and on 24-word sentences only 12.5%. Window widened from 3 because three declarative human sentences hit a low stdev by coincidence (13, 14, 13 gives 0.58). Human copy is bursty.

markers.name: banned dash
markers.why: Em dash and en dash are banned. The hyphen is permitted (his 2026-08-14 relaxation).

markers.name: banned phrase
markers.pattern: \b(quick one|quick question|just a quick|dive in|in today's fast-paced world|it's worth noting|elevate your|unlock (your|the)|leverage(s|d)? (our|your|the)|tapestry|navigating the landscape|game-changer|take it to the next level|peace of mind|one-stop shop|cutting-edge|state-of-the-art|on autopilot|in your words|share (that|your) experience|we would love for you to|thank you for choosing|we value your)\b
markers.why: Named phrase bans. the families in the house wording guide. Includes the customer-service boilerplate close, named by the reviewer on the labelled variant set. 'quick one' and its family added 2026-09-15 on his correction: "stop saying quick one, i never talk like that". It is filler he does not use, and it was written into a text drafted FOR him.

markers.name: determiner tricolon
markers.origin: measured 2026-09-14 on the labelled post-cut variants; the clause tricolon M6 cannot see a noun triple
markers.why: Three parallel noun phrases sharing one determiner: 'your time, your trust, and your style'. The machine isocolon in its commonest form.

markers.name: imperative possessive series
markers.origin: measured 2026-09-14 on the reviewer's 50-sentence scored set; M6 missed it because the clause lengths diverge
markers.why: A repeated imperative-plus-possessive frame: 'Refine your wardrobe, express your individuality, and command respect'. The tell is the frame, not matched length.

markers.name: noun-phrase tricolon
markers.origin: moxies.com read from his screenshots 2026-09-14; measured miss
markers.why: Three consecutive verbless noun-phrase fragments, 2 to 4 words each, at least two carrying an adjective. The machine strapline in its commonest form. M6 sees clause tricolons and M15 needs a shared determiner, so neither can see 'Globally-inspired menus. Welcoming atmosphere. Award-winning hospitality.' A genuine fragment menu carries no adjectives and does not flag.

file_checks.name: no operational boundary
file_checks.origin: external review 2026-09-13 blind spot 1; made structural, external review 2026-09-14
file_checks.why: Copy with zero limits, hours, exclusions, deposits, cancellation terms or payment rules reads as an AI simulation of a business with infinite capacity. TESTED STRUCTURALLY, NOT BY VOCABULARY: a keyword list is spoofed by naming a price, which is how the reviewer's own bypass passed it. A page passes on one of four boundary archetypes or on a concrete posted schedule.

archetypes.B_hard_capacity_ceiling: \b(only|strictly|exclusively|no more than|maximum of|max(imum)? \d|up to \d|limit(ed)? to)\b[^.!?]{0,60}?(\b\d|\b(mon|tues|wednes|thurs|fri|satur|sun)day\b|\bappointment|\bbooking|\bper (day|week|weekend|month))|\bby appointment\b|\bappointment only\b|\bno walk-?ins?\b|\bwalk-?ins?\b[^.!?]{0,40}\b(only|on (mon|tues|wednes|thurs|fri|satur|sun)day)\b|\bminimum\s+(spend|order|purchase|party|group|booking|of)\b|\b(available|valid|offer(ed)?|runs?)\b[^.!?]{0,40}?\b(jan|feb|mar|apr|may|jun|jul|aug|sep|oct|nov|dec)[a-z]*\.?\s*\d{1,2}\b[^.!?]{0,20}?[-‐-―to through until]{1,10}\s*(\b(jan|feb|mar|apr|may|jun|jul|aug|sep|oct|nov|dec)[a-z]*\.?\s*)?\d{1,2}\b
archetypes.D_prerequisite_gate: \b(must|must have|need to|needs to|have to|has to|required to|required|requires?)\b[^.!?]{0,90}?(\b(before|prior to|ahead of|in advance|at drop[- ]?off|when you (drop|bring|come))\b|\b\d[\d,.]*\s*[-‐-―]?\s*(hour|hr|day|week|minute|min|month|dollar|percent|%)\w*\b|\$\s?\d|\b(deposit|retainer|permit|proof of|insurance|photo id|valid id|appointment)\b)|\b(bring|provide|supply)\b[^.!?]{0,60}?\b(before|prior to|when you (drop|bring|come))\b|\b(deposit|retainer|fee|permit|proof of \w+|insurance|photo id|valid id)\b[^.!?]{0,60}?\b(is|are)\s+(required|due|non-?refundable|payable)\b

file_checks.spoof_control: Enjoy zero deposits, flexible hours, and unlimited payments!
file_checks.spoof_note: Must NOT satisfy F1. The old vocabulary list passed it on 'deposits', 'hours' and 'payments'. This string is asserted in the selftest.

archetype_notes.D_widened_2026-09-14: D first required a temporal preposition and therefore called the reviewer's own sentence 5, 'Appointments require a 48-hour deposit of fifty dollars', no boundary. That is a real deposit with a real window and the miss was a FALSE POSITIVE on F1, which is the expensive direction: an F1 that fires on pages that do state limits trains people to ignore it. D now also accepts a requirement verb governing a quantified prerequisite. The spoof stays out because it carries no requirement verb.
archetype_notes.D_passive_order_2026-09-14: D read the requirement verb before the prerequisite only, so the passive order, 'A fifty dollar deposit is required to hold the slot', was called no boundary. Second false positive on F1 in the same build, same direction, pinned in the fixture.
archetype_notes.A_B_widened_2026-09-14_moxies: Third F1 false positive of the day and the same expensive direction. Measured on a real professional restaurant page he called cohesive: 'Available September 8-November 15. Minimum spend and eligibility requirements apply.' carries a date window, a spend floor and an eligibility gate, three real limits, and scored no archetype, so the page was reported as having no operational boundary at all. A carries requirements/restrictions apply and subject-to; B carries a minimum spend and a month-to-month availability window. The spoof stays out: it names no requirement, no minimum and no dates.

file_checks.name: draft residue in copy
file_checks.origin: reviewer a sample site site review 2026-09-13
file_checks.why: Builder scaffolding, prompt residue or placeholder text surviving into visible copy. Measured: a credential card shipped reading 'Her own words on her About page, and the events behind them.'

file_checks.name: asset reused across the page
file_checks.origin: reviewer a sample site site review 2026-09-13
file_checks.why: One image wired into three or more places on a single page. Reads as a thin library rather than a real shoot.

file_checks.name: monotonous grid rhythm
file_checks.origin: reviewer a sample site site review 2026-09-13
file_checks.why: The same two-column split declared four or more times, an alternating 50/50 flip down the whole page. The commonest generated-site cadence.

carve_outs.note: Never flagged. Overcorrection produces copy that reads robotic in reverse.
